messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the fused-attn RFC — ran the sanity harness on the new fused-QKV + bias/rope combo yesterday. posting results and a couple of open questions.

ken: Nice. Was this against the same model shards as the earlier perf runs?

maria: yes, same Llama-variant dev shard, seq_len=1024 baseline. we exercised both fused and fallback paths.

devon: Can you paste the harness summary? links or short logs are fine.

maria: TL;DR: throughput +11% on average for the fused path, p50 latency unchanged, p99 +2.1ms in worst case when rope-offsets misalign. correctness checks (sampled outputs + BLEU-style diff) are clean. failures were limited to one micro-batch path where rope bias reorder triggered an assert in the legacy kernel.

maria: log excerpt:```
[2026-03-18T03:14:06Z] RUN harness/fused-sanity v3
profiles tested: fused-qkv-bias-rope, packed-qkv, fallback
results: fused: thr=1118 tok/s, fallback: thr=1007 tok/s
issues: 1 assert in legacy-kernel qkv_reorder.cpp:line 214 (rope offset mismatch)
```

anya: good numbers. do we have a deterministic repro for that assert? sounds like a rope-offset boundary condition.

maria: i can repro locally with a minimal script; looks like an off-by-one when the sequence crosses a block boundary with caching enabled. working a small patch that clamps offsets.

ken: bigger question: how are we exposing the fused variant to routing? do we gate it behind a kernel-compat flag, model annotation, or runtime auto-select?

devon: my preference is runtime auto-select with explicit fallback policy per route. keep operator contract small: kernel_selector returns {variant: STRING, requires_kv_alignment: BOOL, fallback_score: FLOAT}. that lets the router make cost/latency tradeoffs.

maria: agreed. current prototype returns names like `fused_qkv_bias_rope_v1` and a boolean `rope_aligned=true|false`. if false -> prefer fallback unless latency target is very strict.

liam: we should be careful: auto-select means the binary must carry both fused and fallback kernels and the ABI for KV cache must be stable. how are we versioning that?

maria: plan is to bind kernel id + abi tag in the model manifest (optional). runtime will reject mismatched abi and print a clear error recommending model recompile or runtime upgrade.

ken: can we mitigate with an on-the-fly shim that adapts KV layout for older kernels? might be expensive.

devon: shimming is doable but costly; better to provide cheap conversion helpers for startup time (one-time layout transform) and avoid per-token overhead.

anya: rollout idea: canary 5% traffic to fused for non-critical routes, measure p99 delta, error-rate, and CPU spill. gating thresholds: p99 delta < 5ms, error-rate delta < 0.05%, CPU spill < +10%.

maria: added. also captured a small policy patch for the router to prefer fused when throughput benefit > 7% and estimated p99 impact < 3ms.

sre-bot: Canary job #482 complete: fused-attn canary @5% -> metrics: p50 delta -9%, p99 delta +1.8ms, errors +0.012%, gpu-mem spill +3.1%. Verdict: PASS under current thresholds. :white_check_mark:

liam: nice. one more: what about dropout-less paths? do we need separate codegen for inference-only where dropout ops are dropped entirely?

maria: yes, inference path elides dropout; but that touches kernel signals where dropout toggles layout changes. we keep dropoutless as a compile-time macro in the fused kernel. runtime toggles come from model manifest indicating `training=false`.

ken: doc + operator checklist needed. also need a short runbook for the rope-offset assert repro and the patch.

maria: will open a PR with the patch, harness test, and a runbook itemized steps (how to detect, rollback, and one-liner for the layout clamp). linking here once ready.

devon: can we add a quick unit that fuzzes rope offsets across block boundaries? cheap, would catch these early.

maria: good call — adding fuzz harness now.

anya: schedule: once PR lands, we can flip canary to 20% next week and iterate.

maria: thanks all — will post PR and a short TL;DR for the docs channel.

sre-bot: Deploy plan draft created: https://git.internal/redeploy/plan/9921 - includes rollback steps and metrics dashboard link.
